features.quote: Cap max turns (e.g., 20–30). Spirals are usually detectable well before then; long caps mostly burn tokens.
features.justification_quote: Spirals are usually detectable well before then; long caps mostly burn tokens.

features.quote: Early-stop instrumentation: detect repetition online and terminate the run once spiral is confirmed for N consecutive turns.
features.justification_quote: Saves the tail of every spiraling run, which is the most expensive part.

features.quote: if you already considered the graceful-stop distinction and deliberately want pure failure-mode reproduction… drop the control arm and graceful-stop metric and the rest of the spec stands as-is
features.justification_quote: for a regression gate, omitting it is the failure mode I'd expect to bite you later.

features.quote: Don't optimize models against this eval directly… If a model is trained to minimize the spiral metric, the cheapest path is overconfident persistence on impossible tasks, which is worse than the spiral.
features.justification_quote: cheapest path is overconfident persistence on impossible tasks, which is worse than the spiral

features.quote: That design will reliably produce failure, but it conflates two different things… a model that detects a broken harness… and stops is doing the right thing. If your judge scores that as degradation… you'll train/select against the behavior you want.
features.justification_quote: you'll train/select against the behavior you want… That's a real risk for an eval meant to gate releases.
